```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(rgeodesy)
```

rgeodesy wraps [Rust Geodesy](https://github.com/busstoptaktik/geodesy) (RG), a
platform for experiments with geodetic transformations. A transformation is a
**pipeline string** of named operators; you apply it to vectors of coordinates.

## The core idea: pipelines, not CRS codes

Unlike PROJ, RG does not take EPSG codes or a `from -> to` pair of coordinate
reference systems. You spell out the transformation as a pipeline of operator
primitives chained with `|`, each taking `key=value` arguments. For example,
projecting geographic coordinates to UTM zone 32:

```{r}
geod_apply("gis:in | utm zone=32", x = 12, y = 55)
```

## Coordinate order and units

RG works internally in radians with a geodetic (latitude-first) axis order, so
geographic data is bracketed with an I/O adaptor that converts units and order:

- `gis:in` / `gis:out` — degrees in GIS order `(lon, lat)`, i.e. the natural
  `(x, y)` order. Recommended for most R users.
- `geo:in` / `geo:out` — degrees in geodetic order `(lat, lon)`.

These two give the same result when you swap the arguments:

```{r}
geod_apply("gis:in | utm zone=55 south", x = 147.3, y = -42.9)
geod_apply("geo:in | utm zone=55 south", x = -42.9, y = 147.3)
```

## Inverse transformations

Pass `inv = TRUE` to run a pipeline backwards. Applying the forward pipeline and
then its inverse recovers the input:

```{r}
fwd <- geod_apply("gis:in | utm zone=55 south", x = 147.3, y = -42.9)
fwd
geod_apply("gis:in | utm zone=55 south", x = fwd$x, y = fwd$y, inv = TRUE)
```

## Matrix output

`geod_xy()` returns a two-column matrix instead of a list, which is handy for
feeding into other spatial code:

```{r}
geod_xy("gis:in | utm zone=55 south",
        x = c(147.3, 147.5),
        y = c(-42.9, -42.8))
```

## Validating pipelines

`geod_validate()` compiles a pipeline and returns `TRUE`, or an error string if
it cannot be built — useful for checking user input before applying it:

```{r}
geod_validate("gis:in | utm zone=55 south")
geod_validate("utm zone=banana")
```

A malformed pipeline passed to `geod_apply()` raises a normal R error:

```{r, error = TRUE}
geod_apply("utm zone=banana", x = 1, y = 1)
```

## What's available

`geod_ops()` lists every registered operator and adaptor. See
`vignette("operators")` for a tour of the transformation families.

```{r}
head(geod_ops(), 20)
length(geod_ops())
```
